data.reasoning: Both models correctly identified the PKGBUILD and metadata files as standard AUR packaging with pinned sources and verified checksums. The disagreement is purely due to an API error in the first model that prevented it from reviewing the .gitignore file, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The second model successfully reviewed .gitignore and found it benign. There are no security risks or injected code in the packaging.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen model when attempting to audit .gitignore, forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited the same file and found it safe, resolving the uncertainty.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .gitignore due to an LLM API error.
learnings: The audit tool should implement retry logic for transient API errors to prevent incomplete coverage and unnecessary inconclusive verdicts.
Non-executable files like .gitignore should be flagged as low-risk; a failure to audit them should not block a safe verdict if all executable and packaging files are verified safe.
